claim.why_it_matters: Every sub-entry indent on this page is dropped. The thirteen sub-entries under 'Relation condition' and the three under 'Reserved words' are each promoted to look like top-level index entries. Same systematic defect as pages 1249-1252.

verdict.reasoning:
Independently confirmed at 300 dpi against E:/Temp/specrecon/v1254/spec_p1254.png (printed folio 1224, PDF page 1254 - the standard 30-page front-matter offset) and against the canonical source specs/ISO_COBOL.md lines 52471-52593.

BOTH QUOTES ARE ACCURATE. The rendered PDF shows a two-column back-of-book index with two clearly distinct left margins. Under the flush-left head 'Relation condition' I count exactly thirteen indented sub-entries, in the order and with the page numbers the claim gives: Alphanumeric operands 189, Arithmetic expression in 187, Boolean operands 190, Data-pointer operands 192, Index data item in 187, Index data items 192, Message tags 192, Mixed operands 189, National operands 190, Numeric operands 188, Object reference identifiers 192, Order of evaluation 204, Strongly-typed group items 191. Under the flush-left head 'Reserved words 97, 105' I count exactly three indented sub-entries: Compiler directives 213, Implementation 23, Source text 205. The markdown quote is verbatim from lines 43-47 and 105-108 of the extracted work unit. Neither source is misquoted and no page number is misreported.

THE TEXT IS NOT MERELY REFLOWED. I tested the obvious refutations and all fail. `grep -c '^[ \t]'` over the entire page block returns 0: not one of the ~117 content lines carries a leading space or tab, and `cat -A` confirms no tabs, no list markers, and no   or other entity standing in for the indent. The information is absent from the file in every form, not relocated. This is also not a reading-order or column-break defect: the markdown preserves the left column then the right column in correct order, so the dropped indentation is the sole defect on the page.

DECISIVE EVIDENCE THAT MEANING IS LOST. Markdown lines 40 and 42 are byte-identical: 'REF-MOD-ZERO-LENGTH directive [83](#page-83)'. In the PDF these two lines are visually distinct - line 40 is indented as a sub-entry of 'Reference-modification 131', line 42 is a flush-left top-level entry. The flattening collapses a parent-child relation and a top-level term into an apparent verbatim duplicate. That is unrecoverable structure, not cosmetics: no reader or tool can reconstruct from the markdown which of the two is the sub-entry. In an index the indent IS the content - it is the only encoding of the qualifying parent term. Flattened, 'Implementation 23' asserts an index term 'Implementation' pointing at page 23, when the page actually says 'Reserved words, Implementation -> 23'. Likewise 'Definition 220' becomes a free-floating entry rather than 'Relative files, Definition'. Roughly 55 sub-entries across both columns are promoted this way.

I therefore cannot refute the claim. It survives every disqualifying test in the brief.

CAVEAT ON WEIGHT, NOT ON TRUTH: this is back-of-book index apparatus, not normative text, so no compiler behavior is derived from it. The harm is to lookup fidelity and to any tooling that parses the index into a term hierarchy, plus the false-duplicate artifact above. 'structural' is a fair severity for the defect class; the practical blast radius is navigational.
verdict.corrected_description: Real, and the mechanism is correctly identified, but the label and the scope should be tightened. This is not 'misplaced' content - no text is moved, dropped, or reordered, and the two-column reading order is correct. It is LOST HIERARCHY: the transcription strips leading whitespace from every line, so the PDF's two-level index (flush-left head + indented sub-entry) is flattened to a single level. Verified mechanically: `grep -c '^[ \t]'` over specs/ISO_COBOL.md lines 52471-52593 returns 0 - not one line retains an indent, and no substitute encoding (list marker,  , tab) is used. The claim's two named examples check out exactly (13 sub-entries under 'Relation condition', 3 under 'Reserved words 97, 105'), but they understate the reach: approximately 55 sub-entries across both columns are promoted to apparent top-level terms. The sharpest proof of genuine information loss is a pair the claim does not cite - markdown lines 40 and 42 are byte-identical ('REF-MOD-ZERO-LENGTH directive [83](#page-83)'), whereas the PDF prints line 40 indented under 'Reference-modification 131' and line 42 flush-left as its own entry; the parent-child relation is unrecoverable from the markdown. Consistent with the same systematic transcription defect reported on pages 1249-1252, so it should be fixed as one whole-index sweep rather than page by page. Impact is confined to index navigation and index-parsing tooling: this is non-normative apparatus, so no COBOL semantics are affected.
